'''Stefan Andrus Burr''' (born 1940) is a [[mathematician]] and [[computer scientist]], specializing in [[graph theory]] and [[number theory]], particularly [[Ramsey theory]]. He is a retired professor of [[Computer science|Computer Science]] at [[The City College of New York]].

== Career ==
He did his undergraduate studies at [[University of California, Berkeley]], graduating with a [[Bachelor of Arts]] in Mathematics with Highest Honors in 1961 June.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=June 10, 1961 |title=Certificates, Degrees, and Honors, June 10, 1961: Honors with Degrees: Honors with the Bachelor's Degree: In the College of Letters and Science: Mathematics: Highest Honors |url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=coo.31924065367298&seq=617&q1=burr |journal=Commencement |publisher=University of California |publication-place=California Memorial Stadium, Berkeley |volume=98 |page=135 <!-- "Certificates, Degrees, and Honors, June 10, 1961" starts on p. 64; "Honors with Degrees" starts on p. 132 --> |via=HathiTrust |hdl=2027/coo.31924065367298?urlappend=%3Bseq=617}}</ref> He was a member of their team for the [[William Lowell Putnam Mathematical Competition]] on 1958 November 22, where the team received an honorable mention;<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Bush |first=L. E. |date=August–September 1959 |title=The William Lowell Putnam Mathematical Competition |url=https://archive.org/details/sim_american-mathematical-monthly_august-september-1959_66_7/page/571/mode/2up?q=burr |journal=The American Mathematical Monthly |publisher=Mathematical Association of America |volume=66 |issue=7 |pages=570–572 |doi=10.1080/00029890.1959.11989352 |issn=0002-9890 |jstor=2309855 |via=Internet Archive}}</ref> 1959 November 21, where he individually received an honorable mention;<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Bush |first=L. E. |date=June–July 1960 |title=The William Lowell Putnam Mathematical Competition |url=https://archive.org/details/sim_american-mathematical-monthly_june-july-1960_67_6/page/560/mode/2up?q=Burr |journal=The American Mathematical Monthly |volume=67 |issue=6 |pages=559–561 |doi=10.1080/00029890.1960.11989546 |issn=0002-9890 |jstor=2309174 |via=Internet Archive}}</ref> and 1960 December 3, where the team won first prize and he additionally received an honorable mention.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Bush |first=L. E. |date=August–September 1961 |title=The 1960 William Lowell Putnam Mathematical Competition |url=https://archive.org/details/american-mathematical-monthly-1897-1997-djvu/American%20Mathematical%20Monthly%2C%20vol.068%20%28AMS%2C%201961%29%28600dpi%29%28T%29/page/628/mode/2up?q=burr |journal=The American Mathematical Monthly |volume=68 |issue=7 |pages=629–637 |doi=10.2307/2311508 |issn=0002-9890 |jstor=2311508 |via=Internet Archive}}</ref> As a member of the class of 1961, he received the [[Dorothea Klumpke|Dorothea Klumpke Roberts]] Prize in Mathematics in 1960.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=June 11, 1960 |title=Prizes: Dorothea Klumpke Roberts Prize in Mathematics |url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=uc1.31378008233556&seq=158&q1=burr |journal=Commencement |publisher=University of California |publication-place=California Memorial Stadium, Berkeley |volume=97 |page=146 <!-- Prizes starts on p. 143 --> |via=HathiTrust |hdl=2027/uc1.31378008233556?urlappend=%3Bseq=158}}</ref> As a student there, he joined the [[Mathematical Association of America]] in 1960 April/May.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=May 1960 |title=Official Reports and Communications: New Members |url=https://archive.org/details/american-mathematical-monthly-1897-1997-djvu/American%20Mathematical%20Monthly%2C%20vol.067%20%28AMS%2C%201960%29%28600dpi%29%28T%29/page/494/mode/2up?q=burr |journal=The American Mathematical Monthly |volume=67 |issue=5 |pages=493–497 |doi=10.1080/00029890.1960.11989534 |jstor=2309334 |via=Internet Archive}}</ref>

He graduated from [[Princeton University]] with a [[Master of Arts]] in 1963<ref>{{Cite journal |date=1964 |orig-date=Approved by the Board of Trustees October 25, 1963 |title=Masters of Arts <!-- https://books.google.com/books/content?id=PRFbAAAAYAAJ&pg=PP23&img=1&pgis=1&dq=%22masters+of+arts+approved+by+the+board+of+trustees+october+25+1963+john+francis+regis%22&bul=1&sig=ACfU3U2WmpRD-YmIX0Alj3n_HIdjWPqO8A&edge=0 --> |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PRFbAAAAYAAJ&dq=%22stefan+andrus%22+burr&pg=PP23 |journal=Commencement |publisher=Princeton University |page=23? |via=Google Books}}</ref> and a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in 1968,<ref>{{Cite web |date= |title=Burr, Stefan Andrus, 1968 |url=https://library.princeton.edu/mudd-dbs/graduates?qname=graduate+alumni+index&LASTNAME=Burr&FIRSTNAME=Stefan&YEAR=&department= |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240622201925/https://library.princeton.edu/mudd-dbs/graduates?qname=graduate+alumni+index&LASTNAME=Burr&FIRSTNAME=Stefan&YEAR=&department= |archive-date=2024-06-22 |access-date=2024-06-22 |website=Princeton University Graduate Alumni Index, 1839-1998 |series=Mudd Databases |publisher=The Department of Special Collections, Princeton University Library}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |editor-last=Durgin |editor-first=Lynn |title=Burr, Stefan Andrus, 1968 |url=https://findingaids.princeton.edu/catalog/AC105-04_c3500 |access-date=2024-06-22 |website=Graduate Alumni Records, 1960-1989 |series=Finding Aids |publisher=Princeton University Archives, Department of Special Collections, Princeton University Library |publication-date=2018 |id=AC105-04}}</ref> both in Mathematics. His PhD thesis, ''An Elementary Solution of the [[Waring–Goldbach problem|Waring-Goldbach Problem]]'' (1968 or 1969)<ref>{{Cite thesis |last=Burr |first=Stefan Andrus |title=An elementary solution of the Waring-Goldbach problem |date=1968 |degree=Ph.D. |publisher=Princeton University |id={{ProQuest|302326486}}. [[Dissertation Abstracts International|DAI]]-B PRIN [https://books.google.com/books/content?id=Z5QgAQAAMAAJ&pg=PA207&img=1&pgis=1&dq=%22stefan+andrus%22&bul=1&sig=ACfU3U2RDXAwiAXYuqf3WnMM-z6hxaBGjg&edge=0 29/088/2967] <!-- not sure about the 088, since the Google Books preview is too blurry -->, [https://books.google.com/books/content?id=tVZFAQAAIAAJ&pg=PA2967&img=1&pgis=1&dq=%22princeton+university,+1968%22+burr&bul=1&sig=ACfU3U2v1JUWdnLQF_FmbAfyw8nZvRvieA&edge=0 69-2530]. |mr=2617568 |isbn=9781085008488 |oclc=39118789 |url=https://catalog.princeton.edu/catalog/9919647883506421}}</ref> was advised by [[Bernard Dwork|Bernard Morris Dwork]].<ref name="mg">{{Cite web |title=Stefan Andrus Burr |url=https://mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=28377 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200701080059/http://mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=28377 |archive-date=2020-07-01 |access-date=2024-06-22 |website=[[Mathematics Genealogy Project]] |publisher=Department of Mathematics, North Dakota State University |publication-place=Fargo, North Dakota}}<!-- {{mathgenealogy|name=Stefan Andrus Burr|id=28377}} but with more information --></ref>

While working on his PhD at Princeton, he had a job as a Scientific Programmer for [[Lockheed Corporation|Lockheed]] MSC ({{Circa|1965}}).<ref>{{Cite journal |date=October 1, 1965 |title=Individual Members: Alphabetical Listing: Burr, Stefan A. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=CcTuAAAAMAAJ&dq=burr&pg=PA70 |journal=Combined Membership List of the American Mathematical Society and the Mathematical Association of America |volume=1965-1966 |page=70 |via=Google Books}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Forbes |first=Donald |date=October 1988 |title=Desktop Publishing |url=https://archive.org/details/jacg198810/page/n5?q=%22stefan+andrus%22+burr |journal=Jersey Atari Computer Group (JACG) Newsletter |publication-place=Pine Brook, New Jersey |volume=8 |issue=8 |page=[5] |via=Internet Archive}}</ref> Afterwards, starting {{Circa|1966}}, he had a job as a member of the technical staff at [[Bell Labs|Bell Telephone Laboratories]],<ref>{{Cite journal |date=October 1, 1966 |title=Individual Members: Alphabetical Listing: Burr, Stefan A. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=rT9VAAAAYAAJ&dq=burr&pg=RA2-PA218 |journal=Combined Membership List of the American Mathematical Society and the Mathematical Association of America |volume=1966-1967 |page=218 |via=Google Books}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |date=May 1, 1967 |title=Individual Members: Alphabetical Listing: Burr, Stefan A. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ecU_AQAAIAAJ&dq=burr&pg=PA26 |journal=Combined Membership List of the American Mathematical Society and the Mathematical Association of America |volume=1967-1968 |page=26 |via=Google Books}}</ref><ref>{{Cite conference |last=Burr |first=Stefan A. |date=18-23 August 1969 |editor-last=Atkin |editor-first=Oliver |editor-link=A. O. L. Atkin |editor2-last=Birch |editor2-first=Bryan John |editor2-link=Bryan John Birch |title=A Class of Theorems in Additive Number Theory which Lend Themselves to Computer Proof |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=dBDvAAAAMAAJ&dq=%22Themselves+to+Computer+Proof+%22&pg=PA283 |conference=Computers in Number Theory conference |series=Science Research Council Atlas Symposium |publication-place=Oxford |publication-date=1971 |volume=2 |issue= |page=283 |via=Google Books}}

Many of his publications involve problems from the field of [[Ramsey theory]].  He has published 27 papers with [[Paul Erdős]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html|title=Paul Erdős' papers|publisher=Alfréd Rényi Institute of Mathematics|accessdate=25 October 2022}}</ref> The [[Burr–Erdős conjecture]], published as a conjecture by Burr and Erdős in 1975, solved only in 2015, states that [[sparse graph]]s have [[linear growth|linearly growing]] [[Ramsey number]]s.
